subject: Human Evolution
title: Buffalo Jumps
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Buffalo Jumps.

hook.text: At Head-Smashed-In, Alberta, bison bones pile ten meters deep at the base of a cliff. Thousands died here.

buildup.text: Hunters drove herds toward hidden cliffs using fire, noise, and stampede lanes made of stone cairns.

discovery.text: A single drive could kill hundreds of animals at once—more meat than spear hunting could deliver.

twist.text: This required weeks of planning, terrain preparation, and coordination among dozens of people.

climax.text: Buffalo jumps show that ice age hunters engineered landscapes for mass food production.

punchline.text: Gravity was the most efficient weapon.

quiz.question: What were buffalo jumps?
options: Planned drives that stampeded herds over cliffs for mass kills
